body.statement: Suppose \(\Delta_T=0\) and \(\beta=q=(1-\alpha)/2\). Uniformly on \(\mathfrak M_{T,0}^{\mathrm{reg}}(\kappa)\), \(I_{T,0}^{\mathrm G}\) has asymptotic coverage at least \(1-\eta\). For deterministic \(\pi_t(1)=ct^{-\alpha}\), there is a Rademacher immediate-outcome plus finite hidden-sign delay family in the same experiment for which \((\widehat\tau_{T,0}-\tau)/s_{T,0}\Rightarrow N(-u,1)\) and \(B_{T,0}/s_{T,0}\to u>0\); for every fixed \(c'>0\), the limiting coverage of \([\widehat\tau_{T,0}\pm c'\widehat s_{T,0}]\) equals \(\Phi(c'-u)+\Phi(c'+u)-1\). Hence \(c_\eta(u)\) is attained for symmetric intervals at the phase boundary.
body.justification: The result converts the phase boundary into an attained local experiment rather than a conservative bias comparison.
body.gap: Armstrong and Kolesár supply the generic bounded-bias Gaussian calibration, while delayed-bandit work does not derive or attain its bias ratio in the adaptive observed experiment.
body.consumer: This gives trial statisticians the correct critical value when the endpoint-tail and exploration exponents meet at the nonzero-shift boundary.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(Z\sim N(0,1)\). For \(c>0\) and \(v\geq0\),
\[
 P\{|Z-v|\leq c\}=\Phi(c-v)+\Phi(c+v)-1. \tag{21}
\]
The derivative of the right side in \(v\) is \(\phi(c+v)-\phi(c-v)\leq0\). Hence the least coverage over shifts of absolute value at most \(u\) occurs at the endpoint \(u\). For fixed \(u\), the right side of (21) is continuous and strictly increasing in \(c\), from zero to one. This proves existence and uniqueness of \(c_\eta(u)\), and its defining equation gives exact coverage \(1-\eta\) at the endpoint shift.

Now suppose \(\Delta_T=0\) and \(\beta=q\). On the regular class, the variance comparison (9) in the gated-inference proof and the regular-variance assumption imply
\[
 0<c_0T^{-2q}\leq s_{T,0}^2\leq C_0T^{-2q} \tag{22}
\]
uniformly. The old-cohort correction lemma gives \(B_{T,0}=O(T^{-q})\), so \(B_{T,0}/s_{T,0}\) is uniformly bounded. Uniform studentization, \(\widehat s_{T,0}/s_{T,0}\to1\), the uniform Lipschitz property of \(f_B(s)=s c_\eta(B/s)\) established in the gated-inference proof, and \(|b_{T,0}|\leq B_{T,0}\) imply from (21) that
\[
 \inf_{(P,\Pi,T)\in\mathfrak M_{T,0}^{\mathrm{reg}}(\kappa)}
 P\{\tau\in I_{T,0}^{\mathrm G}\}\geq1-\eta-o(1).
\]
The added radius \(d_{T,0}=o(T^{-q})=o(s_{T,0})\) is nonnegative and does not change the limiting endpoint calibration.

We construct an attaining triangular family. Use the deterministic policy \(\pi_t(1)=ct^{-\alpha}\) and put
\[
 \delta_T=L(1+T)^{-q}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(T\), so that \(\delta_T<1/2\). Index the two alternatives by \(\zeta\in\{-1,1\}\). In arm one, with probability \(\delta_T\), set \((D,Y)=(T+1,\zeta)\); conditional on \(D=0\), let \(Y\in\{-1,1\}\) have mean \(-\zeta\delta_T/(1-\delta_T)\). In arm zero, with probability \(\delta_T\), set \((D,Y)=(T+1,-\zeta)\); conditional on \(D=0\), let \(Y\in\{-1,1\}\) have mean \(\zeta\delta_T/(1-\delta_T)\). The two arms may be taken independent within each arrival vector, and the vectors are independent and identically distributed over recruitment times.

These laws have bounded outcomes and finite delays. For integer \(u\leq T\), their delay tail is \(\delta_T\leq L(1+u)^{-q}\), and it is zero for \(u\geq T+1\), so the polynomial envelope holds without outcome--delay independence. In each arm the visible and hidden means cancel, while \(Y^2=1\); hence
\[
 PY(1)=PY(0)=0,
 \qquad \operatorname{Var}_P(Y(1))=\operatorname{Var}_P(Y(0))=1. \tag{23}
\]
Thus the family is in the regular class whenever its variance floor is support-feasible, namely \(\kappa\leq1\) for \(\alpha>0\) and \(\kappa\leq2\) for \(\alpha=0\); for larger \(\kappa\) that regular class is empty by bounded support.

Because \(g_{T,0}<h_{T,0}<T+1\), every correction variable is zero. For \(\zeta=1\),
\[
 \tau=0,
 \qquad b_{T,0}=2\delta_T,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(X_{a,1}^{0})=1-\delta_T-\delta_T^2,
\]
and therefore
\[
 s_{T,0}^2=(1-\delta_T-\delta_T^2)(K_1^{-1}+K_0^{-1}). \tag{24}
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \frac{b_{T,0}}{B_{T,0}}
 =\left(\frac{1+h_{T,0}}{1+T}\right)^q\longrightarrow1. \tag{25}
\]
The quota asymptotics in (24) now yield
\[
 \frac{B_{T,0}}{s_{T,0}}\longrightarrow u=
 \begin{cases}
 2L\sqrt{c/(1-\alpha)},&\alpha>0,\\
 2L(c^{-1}+\varepsilon^{-1})^{-1/2},&\alpha=0,
 \end{cases} \tag{26}
\]
which is finite and strictly positive. The bounded independent triangular-array calculation used in (4), together with quota success and sample-variance consistency, gives
\[
 \frac{\widehat\tau_{T,0}-\tau+b_{T,0}}{s_{T,0}}\Rightarrow N(0,1),
 \qquad \frac{\widehat s_{T,0}}{s_{T,0}}\longrightarrow1.
\]
Combining this with (25)--(26) proves
\[
 \frac{\widehat\tau_{T,0}-\tau}{s_{T,0}}\Rightarrow N(-u,1),
 \qquad \frac{B_{T,0}}{s_{T,0}}\longrightarrow u.
\]
Since \(\tau=0\) is in the interior of \([-2,2]\) and all radii vanish, truncation at the parameter-space boundary is asymptotically irrelevant. Thus for every fixed \(c'>0\),
\[
 P\{\tau\in[\widehat\tau_{T,0}\pm c'\widehat s_{T,0}]\}
 \longrightarrow \Phi(c'-u)+\Phi(c'+u)-1.
\]
By (21), \(c'=c_\eta(u)\) gives equality \(1-\eta\), and every smaller symmetric critical value gives strictly smaller endpoint-shift coverage. This proves attainment in the delayed adaptive experiment.
